Route 1 confirms independently: paper Table 2 (image t002) M/SD vs live M/SD -- 'intrusive gesture' 3.27/1.18 vs Touching 3.274/1.182; 'contact with professionals is pleasant' 3.77/1.02 vs Contact_with_professionals 3.767/1.022; 'very unpleasant ... unknown people' 4.00/1.17 vs Contact_with_unknown 3.997/1.168. Largest |dM|=0.0038, |dSD|=0.0024; n=1143/1145/1146. Every item is distinguished from every other: published means are 3.27, 3.77, 4.00 (gaps 0.50 and 0.23, vs residuals under 0.004), and each item's nearest published (M,SD) row is its own. Route 6 corroborates: the two aversive statements correlate +0.406, and each correlates negatively with the approving one (-0.134, -0.069), so data are raw and polarity matches the text. Option axis rests on the Methods sentence 1='I strongly disagree' to 5='I strongly agree'; 2-4 unlabelled and blank.

Route 3 (published subscale descriptives): canonical MSLQ key applied to live items reproduces all 15 subscales in the deposit's Table 3/Table 4 (n=347 each). M obs vs pub: IGO 5.246/5.24, EGO 5.317/5.31, TV 6.004/6.00, CB 5.518/5.51, SE 5.270/5.27, TA 5.082/5.08, REH 5.367/5.36, ELA 5.133/5.13, ORG 5.385/5.38, CT 5.020/5.02, MSR 5.096/5.09, TSE 4.871/4.87, ER 4.722/4.72, PL 4.107/4.10, HS 5.287/5.28 (published M appear truncated); SD all within 0.008 (e.g. MSR .709/.708, TSE .566/.565); min/max exact to 2dp on all 15 (e.g. MSR 2.917-6.417 vs 2.92-6.42, TSE 3.625-5.875 vs 3.63-5.88, TA 1.20-7.00, PL 1.333-7.00). Reverse-keying the 8 canonical reverse items breaks MSR/TSE/ER/HS (e.g. TSE min 2.25 vs 3.63), so items are raw. Supporting but non-statistical: codes itemN share numbering with questionnaire items N, which follow canonical MSLQ order.
